title: Reviewing the declaration line by line

exchanges.q: Today we will review your declaration line by line. Is that okay?
Paragraph three says you were detained for two days. Is that right?
exchanges.a: No, it was four days. Two days at the police station and two days at another place.

exchanges.q: Paragraph five says your brother was a witness. Is that correct?
exchanges.a: Yes. My brother {BROTHER} saw everything from the window.

exchanges.q: You wrote that you applied for a visa in 2019. What kind of visa?
exchanges.a: A tourist visa. They denied it at the interview.

exchanges.q: Have you ever applied for asylum in another country?
exchanges.a: No, never. I only passed through {TRANSIT_COUNTRY} for three days.

exchanges.q: The declaration says the threats started in 2020. When did they start exactly?
a: The first threat was in December 2019, by phone.
The threats in person started in February 2020.

exchanges.q: Who wrote the letter from the doctor?
exchanges.a: Doctor {DOCTOR}, at the clinic in {CITY}. He treated my ribs after the attack.

exchanges.q: Are you sure the attack was in June?
exchanges.a: I think it was June, but it could be the beginning of July. It was right after my birthday.

exchanges.q: Did you sign anything at the police station?
exchanges.a: Yes, they made me sign a statement, but they did not let me read it.

exchanges.q: Is there anything in the declaration you want to change?
exchanges.a: Only the number of days I was detained, and that the threats started in December.
